issues.body: `resolve_local_branch()` accepts any name returned under `refs/heads/`, but it does not establish that this is a direct ref. Git allows (including via `git symbolic-ref`) `refs/heads/ledger-purge` to point at `refs/remotes/origin/ledger`. The accepted name remains `refs/heads/ledger-purge`, while ref updates ordinarily dereference symbolic refs; filter-branch can consequently move the remote-tracking target through the accepted alias. The tests cover shorthand resolution but no symbolic-ref alias, so the stated one-local-branch boundary is still bypassable.
issues.fix_hint: Before scanning or invoking filter-branch, require the resolved `refs/heads/...` name to be a direct ref (refuse it if `git symbolic-ref -q <full-name>` succeeds), and keep using the validated full name. Add a real fixture whose `refs/heads/...` symbolic ref targets `refs/remotes/origin/ledger`; assert rewrite refuses before creating `refs/original/` and that both the target and alias remain unchanged, alongside the existing direct-local-branch accept case.
issues.title: A symbolic ref under refs/heads can redirect the rewrite outside the local branch namespace

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Both round-1 findings are materially addressed: rewrite operations now use a resolved full ref, and commit records use NUL framing with real control-byte coverage. However, the local-only boundary still trusts the namespace spelling without rejecting symbolic refs. Git permits a ref under `refs/heads/` to be symbolic; updates through such a ref normally dereference it. A crafted local-looking symbolic ref can therefore point at `refs/remotes/origin/ledger`, pass `resolve_local_branch()`, and let filter-branch update the remote-tracking ref that the guard promises never to touch. This is a new major trust-boundary finding, so progress is regressing under the required scale.
